Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Bengaluru Instituted
Against The Petitioner For Offence P/U/S.419, 420, 468,
471, 120-B, 204 R/W Sec.34 Of Ipc.
 This Criminal Petition, Coming On For Orders,
This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

Petitioners are before this Court calling in question the proceedings in C.C.No.4972/2021 (Crime No.487 of 2018) for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 468, 471, 120B, 204 r/w Section 34 of the IPC.

During the pendency of the petition, the parties to the lis have settled the dispute amicably amongst themselves and have filed an application under Section 482 and 320(2) of the Cr.P.C.
seeking to compound the offences.

The compromise entered into insofar as the present petition is concerned reads as follows:
 ".... .... ....
 4) That, the offence so alleged in C.C.No.4972/2021 on the file of learned 31st Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore for the offences punishable under Section - 419, 420, 468, 471, 120B, 204 read with Section - 34 IPC Smt. Chikkamma vs State Of Karnataka on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139703518/
2 are not compoundable without the permission of the court.

entities.text: Smt. Chikkamma vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the settlement between the Petitioners and second Respondent the above criminal petition is liable to be allowed and the criminal prosecution initiated therein requires to be quashed.
Otherwise, the Petitioners and second Respondent will be put to greater inconvenience, irreparable loss and damage and also hardship and injustice.
If permission granted it may not cause any hardship to the first Respondent or to the state.

5) It is further submitted that the impact of the allegation made by the second Respondent against the Petitioners is not an offence alleged to have committed against the state, but it is only against an individual particularly the second Respondent."
NC: 2023:KHC:21143 3.

Since the offences alleged against the petitioners are under Sections 419, 420, 468, 471, 120B, 204 r/w Section 34 of the IPC, which are not against the State or the Society, and in the light of the compromise arrived at between the parties as aforesaid, I deem it appropriate to obliterate the proceedings pending against the petitioners.
4. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER (i) Criminal Petition is disposed.
(ii) Impugned proceedings in C.C.No.4972/2021 pending before the 31st Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore stands quashed qua the petitioners.
Sd/-
